cards.details: Alexander crosses the Hindu Kush, entering the Kabul Valley to secure the frontiers of the Persian Empire.
The historic Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum) against King Porus; the first major encounter with Indian war elephants.
Alexander reaches the confluence of the Indus and starts his retreat via Gedrosia, ending the Hellenistic campaign in India.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks
mnemonics.description: Remember the sequence and key entities.

items.title: P-A-K
items.decryption: Remember the primary Indian stakeholders: Ambhi (Taxila) surrendered, Porus (Paurava) resisted, and the Kathas fought fiercely.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing the Battle of Hydaspes with the Battle of Gaugamela; Hydaspes was fought against Porus, not Darius III.
Assuming Alexander conquered the entire Magadhan Empire; he stopped at the Hyphasis (Beas) river due to mutiny.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Khyber Pass: Primary entry point.
  • Hydaspes (Jhelum): Site of the decisive battle.
  • Hyphasis (Beas): The limit of the Macedonian expansion.

Personalities

  • Alexander: The Macedonian King.
  • Ambhi: Ruler of Taxila, first collaborator.
  • Porus: Heroic defender of the Jhelum region.

Strategic Overview

  • Political Fragmentation: Alexander exploited the disunity among the frontier kingdoms.
  • Military Innovation: Use of Phalanx formation against elephant corps.
  • Impact:
    • Facilitated political unification (Chandragupta Maurya).
    • Increased trade routes and cultural exchange (Gandhara Art origins).
